reasoning_traces.think:
The AWS compatibility index operates as a dual-layered constraint system: first, it enforces a canonical mapping (S → E), ensuring that all local documentation aligns with authoritative AWS sources. Second, it applies a boundary condition (B) that excludes live operations, thereby preventing accidental exposure or misconfiguration. The compatibility index (I) acts as a derived kernel that validates this alignment through local checks. The shadow boundary (B) enforces a logical partitioning of allowable actions, ensuring that even if the index is valid, no unauthorized behavior can occur. Together, these primitives define a closed-loop system where evidence integrity and operational safety coexist. Failure modes include index corruption (invalid I), boundary violation (B fails), or unauthorized action execution (A \ L).
